:::caution[The Mug↔cup loop this verifies is retired — the PROBE still works]
`cup:spawn` **refuses** as of 2026-08-09; the Mug · Kettle · Cup tier is
[retired](/internal/docs/agent-insights/mug-kettle-cup-tier-is-retired), so there is no
Mug↔cup reporting loop left to prove. Kept because the underlying failure is not
cup-specific and is still live: **an agent can do its file work perfectly and be
coordination-MUTE**, because its platform MCP tools are deferred behind ToolSearch and a
degraded backend writes under the wrong identity. Any spawned agent can fail this way.
Re-point the probe by dropping the `child_role='cup'` predicate (or setting it to the role
you actually launched) — the `coord_event_log.body->>'from'` ⋈ `spawned_agents.session_owner`
join is unchanged.
:::

## The mistake this prevents

"The cup ran, its files landed, tests are green — the spawn works." **That
tells you nothing about whether the cup could *report*.** A spawned cup has
two halves: it does work (file edits) **and** it coordinates (coord:send
acks, plan-item flips, wake-sends, friction capture). The second half can be
**entirely missing** while the first looks perfect — the cup is
*coordination-mute* (EI-75: 0 coord rows across ~15 cups/cups, every one of
which edited files fine).

You will not catch this from a unit-test suite or by eyeballing the cup's
output. The cup even *thinks* it reported — it wrote a `coord:send`-shaped
HTTP call. It just went to the wrong place under the wrong identity.

## Why it happens

A cup:spawn cup's platform tools (`mcp__papercusp__<group>_<verb>`) are
**DEFERRED** behind Claude Code's ToolSearch — they are not eager-loaded into
the tool list. A small/cheap backend (often haiku) that doesn't know the
contract concludes *"I don't have a way to call MCP tools,"* writes a bash
script, and `curl`s the operator's HTTP routes — self-identifying by the
**Run ID** its prompt showed, not its real **Spawn ID**. Result: the write is
rejected (auth) or lands under a forked identity (EI-311), never under the
cup's `spawned_agents.session_owner`. The Mug, querying by session_owner,
sees silence and must do per-cup psql/git archaeology instead.

The fix is the **deferred-tools recipe**, which now lives in TWO places:

1. A **role-generic block baked into every spawned role's prompt**
   (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/prompt-build.ts` §2d, guarded by
   a test in `prompt-build.test.ts`): *load via one ToolSearch select, then
   CALL the tools directly; if MCP is genuinely unusable after reload+retry,
   fall back to the sanctioned `scripts/mcp-call.mjs` helper — NEVER raw
   HTTP/curl, which is not attributed to your identity and corrupts fleet
   state.* This is unconditional — every role gets it, not just cup.
2. Previously ALSO a per-role playbook file, `apps/operator/prompts/bee.tools.md`,
   read at spawn time (`invoke.ts` § "Cross-tool playbook",
   `${promptsDir}/${role}.tools.md`, best-effort). **That file was deleted in
   the pot-rename and no `cup.tools.md` replaced it** — `existsSync` on the
   per-role path is best-effort, so a cup spawned today gets ONLY the §2d
   role-generic block above, no cup-specific playbook section. If you are
   debugging a coordination-mute cup, do not go looking for a
   `cup.tools.md`/`cup.tools.md` file — it doesn't exist; the recipe is
   entirely in the shared §2d preamble now.

## The verification probe (the part that's non-obvious)

A code fix to the prompt is necessary but **not sufficient** — cups spawn
from the GREEN `:3070` release checkout, so a staging prompt fix only takes
effect once it deploys. The only honest close criterion is operational. Run
this against the live DB (resolve the URL from `$PAPERCUSP_DATABASE_URL` /
`getHarnessAdminUrl`):

```sql
-- coord writes authored by a cup under its REAL identity, last 48h
SELECT count(*),
       count(DISTINCT s.spawn_id)            AS distinct_cups,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.writer_key IS NOT NULL) AS mcp_attributed
FROM harness_shared.coord_event_log e
JOIN harness_shared.spawned_agents s
  ON e.body->>'from' = s.session_owner
WHERE s.child_role = 'cup'
  AND s.started_at > now() - interval '48 hours';
```

(Older rows may still show `child_role = 'cup'` if your window predates the
pot-rename backfill — check both if probing a period spanning the migration.)

- **0** → still mute (the EI-75 condition).
- **Non-zero with `writer_key` set on (nearly) all rows** → the loop is alive,
  via the authenticated MCP path. A `writer_key IS NULL` row is the degraded
  curl path — count those separately; they signal a cup that fell back.
- Bucket by `date_trunc('day', e.ts)` to *see the 0→nonzero transition* line up
  with the deploy — that's what distinguishes "fixed" from "always worked."

Watch the join key: it is `body->>'from' = session_owner`, **not** `run_id`.
Coord rows whose `from` is `s-1781…` may be interactive engineer shells
(omp-hook-session), which do **not** join `spawned_agents` — don't count them
as cup activity.

## Rules of thumb

- **A green test run does not prove a spawned agent can coordinate.** Tests check
  the prompt *contains* the recipe; only the live coord-by-session_owner probe
  proves a real cup *used* it.
- **Prompt fixes for spawned roles ride the release gate to `:3070`.** Re-run the
  probe *after the next green deploy*; verifying on staging proves nothing about
  the host cups actually spawn from.
- **`writer_key` is your authenticity signal.** Set = the attributed MCP path;
  NULL = a bare-curl degradation worth chasing.
- **Role ids renamed (D-007):** `bee`→`cup`, `queen`→`mug`, `sentinel`→`papercup`,
  `overwatch`→`kettle`. `canonicalCoordRole()`
  (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/roles.ts`) is the
  reusable old→new mapping if you need to normalize a mixed-era query.
